paper_title: Dark matter detection using nuclear magnetization in magnet with hyperfine interaction
suggested_experiment_name: MnCO₃ canted antiferromagnet nuclear magnetization detector
notes: This is a theoretical proposal paper presenting sensitivity projections, NOT measured exclusion limits. The paper proposes using a canted antiferromagnet MnCO3 with strong hyperfine interaction to detect axions and dark photons via nuclear magnon excitation. Primary results are sensitivity projections (Figs. 7–9) for: (1) axion-proton coupling g_ap at ~10^−6 eV with sensitivity ~10^−11 (nuclear-dominated mode, 500–600 MHz); (2) axion-electron coupling g_ae at ~10^−6 eV with sensitivity ~10^−14; (3) dark photon kinetic mixing ϵ. The paper explicitly states these are projections for a 1 kg MnCO3 sample at T=0.1K with 1-year observation time. The coupling_type is set to AxionProton because the nuclear spin of 55Mn is primarily sensitive to proton spin (σ_p ≈ 0.1, σ_n ≈ 0) per Appendix A. The data_points represent the approximate mass range (10^−6 to 10^−5 eV) and sensitivity floor (~10^−11) from Fig. 7 for the nuclear-dominated mode. The dm_density_assumed (0.4 GeV/cm³) is the standard galactic DM density used throughout the paper (Eq. 2.12). Extraction confidence is moderate (0.65) because: (i) the paper discusses multiple coupling types (AxionProton, AxionElectron, DarkPhoton) and the primary focus shifts between them; (ii) the sensitivity curves are projections with several assumptions (relaxation times, sample mass, temperature, readout efficiency); (iii) no actual measured data or exclusion limits are presented.
